pairs.evidence: src/features/overview/sub_leaderboard/libs/leaderboardScoring.ts:168 computeLeaderboard gives gold/silver/bronze by position in an argmax sort of a composite score built from noisy live telemetry rates; nothing tests whether rank 1 is actually separated from rank 2, so a one-point lead gets the winner medal (the 'argmax winner' failure mode).

techniques.evidence: src/features/overview/sub_leaderboard/libs/leaderboardScoring.ts:168 Medals are a winner label taken from sort position alone. There is no separation test, no interval per persona and no grouping of indistinguishable personas, which the technique requires once an ordering is presented as a conclusion.
src/features/overview/sub_leaderboard/libs/leaderboardScoring.ts:20 The input is per-persona aggregate health signals, with no case set and no per-case scores, so there is nothing to pair.

src/features/overview/sub_leaderboard/libs/useLeaderboardData.ts:6 The 'benchmark' is a live fleet mean recomputed on every render, not a stored baseline, so there are no conditions that could go stale.

src/features/overview/sub_leaderboard/libs/leaderboardScoring.ts:68 The only threshold is a compile-time coverage floor on measured weight. It is not a significance level, and no confidence setting exists.

src/features/overview/sub_leaderboard/libs/leaderboardScoring.ts:136 There are no halting eval runs here. Unmeasured dimensions are null, not zero (in the spirit of 'skipped is not zero'), but the technique's precondition, a run that can halt partway, does not hold.
src/features/overview/sub_leaderboard/libs/leaderboardScoring.ts:166 There is no pipeline or exit code. The closest analogue is that an unranked state stays separate from a rank.

src/features/overview/sub_leaderboard/libs/leaderboardRanking.ts:49 rankBy re-medals across 6 orderings, which is a family of claims, but no statistical test exists to correct. The missing test is recorded under tested-superiority-claims, so it is not counted twice.

pairs.registryProposal: tested-superiority-claims says it attaches whenever 'an ordering is presented as a conclusion', but its procedure assumes per-case eval data. It does not say what a leaderboard over operational telemetry (success rate, latency, cost, with no shared case set) should do. Its decision rule 'no comparable pairing -> say not comparable' would forbid medals entirely there. A sentence covering ranking over non-pairable telemetry (per-candidate intervals or clustering by sample count) would settle whether such surfaces are in scope.

techniques.evidence: src/features/agents/sub_lab/components/arena/ArenaResultsView.tsx:201 An untested 'Best' badge on the argmax model. The arenaWinnerScore.ts:36 argmax (`if (!best || comp > best.comp)`) feeds the history 'winner scores' column the same way.

src/features/agents/sub_lab/components/arena/ArenaResultsView.tsx:84 The summary picks the most extreme pair (best vs worst) after seeing the means and prints 'outperforming {worst} by {gap} points'. src/features/agents/sub_lab/components/arena/ArenaHistory.tsx:168 This is an interactive UI with no pipeline step or exit codes. Run status only gates the export and improve actions.
